dict.string: Blink looks at your calendar only when you turn on the Calendar switch in Settings, so chats can answer questions like “What’s on my Thursday?” Nothing is read until you allow it, and every lookup is shown in the app’s activity log.

Blink looks at your calendar only when you turn on the Calendar switch in Settings, so chats can answer questions like “What’s on my Thursday?” Nothing is read until you allow it, and every lookup is shown in the app’s activity log.

Blink looks at your reminders only when you turn on the Reminders switch in Settings, so chats can tell you what’s still on your list. Nothing is read until you allow it, and every lookup is shown in the app’s activity log.

Blink looks at your reminders only when you turn on the Reminders switch in Settings, so chats can tell you what’s still on your list. Nothing is read until you allow it, and every lookup is shown in the app’s activity log.

Blink looks up a contact only when you turn on the Contacts switch in Settings and a chat needs a phone number or email you asked for. Nothing is read until you allow it, and every lookup is shown in the app’s activity log.

Blink looks at your photo library only when you turn on the Photos switch in Settings — to list recent photos, read the text in one, or make a smaller copy when you approve it. Your photos are never changed; resized copies are new files. Every lookup is shown in the app’s activity log.

Blink searches your music library only when you turn on the Music switch in Settings, so chats can find a song by title, artist, or album. Nothing is read until you allow it, and every lookup is shown in the app’s activity log.

Blink asks Finder which files you have selected, only while the Shared folders switch is on, so the quick panel (⌘⇧Space) can act on “this file”. Nothing is sent anywhere — the selection is only shown to the model answering you.
